d: The animation graph editor is a visual, node-based tool that lets you build complex animation logic.
h:
The Animation Graph Editor is a visual, node-based tool that empowers technical artists and animators to build complex animation logic directly within Roblox Studio. By providing a streamlined interface for creating behaviors like blend trees, it removes the traditional dependency on manual scripting for character motion.

This system works in tandem with your existing animation workflow:

  • Animation Editor: Continue using the Animation Editor as your primary tool for authoring individual clips and fine-tuning keyframes and curves.
  • Animation Graph Editor: Use this tool to take those clips and organize them into a logic tree to drive sophisticated gameplay behavior.

Designed to enhance collaboration, the visual graph allows developers to quickly inspect, debug, and understand the logic created by animators. While artists focus on refining interactive motion, developers can still access animation graph nodes programmatically for direct control over blended animations and states.

Build a graph

Watch this video on YouTube ↗

To begin building logic for an animatable character, access the Animation Graph editor via the Avatar tab in the Studio ribbon. The following steps demonstrate how to initialize a rig and construct a basic node network using default walking and waving animations.

For a deeper dive into practical applications, you can explore the Animation Graph Reference File, which contains both foundational and complex implementation examples.

To create your own animation graph, similar to the basic example provided in the reference, use the following steps:

  1. In Studio, add an animatable rig by navigating to the Avatar tab and selecting Character ⟩ My Avatar.

  1. Open the Animation Graph Editor by navigating to Graph Editor in the Avatar tab.

  1. Select the animatable rig in the 3D viewport. In the graph edtior view, select Graph in the top left corner and select New to create a new graph.
  2. In the Graph Editor, right-click and select Insert Node ⟩ Clip.

  1. In the new Clip node, set the Animation ID.
  2. Select the Animation ID dropdown.

  3. To submit a specific animation asset ID, click Import.

  4. In the Animation ID field, add the default Walk animation: 507777826.

  5. Select Import.

  6. Add another clip node by repeating steps 4-5 using the default Wave animation: 507770239.

  1. In the Graph Editor, right-click and select Add.

  1. Connect the Clip nodes to the Add node by dragging the top-right output connector to the appropriate port:
  2. Connect the Clip node with the Walking animation to the Base port.

  3. Connect the Clip node with the Waving animation to the Additive port.

  4. From the Add node, connect the top-right output connector to the Graph Output Pose port.

  1. OPTIONAL Assign a parameter to your Speed variable.

    1. Click and drag the green Speed port to an empty area. A new parameter node displays.

    2. In the top left of the graph editor, use the parameter pane to quickly modify parameters in your nodes. You can also access this programmatically.

  2. Test the animation by pressing the play button.

  3. Try testing various weights, speeds, playmodes, and other animations. For more information on individual nodes, see the Node reference.

Check out the reference place for different examples of various animation graph configurations.

API integration

Creating and deploying an Animation Graph follows the standard Roblox animation pipeline. After selecting a rig in the Animation Graph Editor, a new AnimationGraphDefinition asset is created. This asset serves as the container for your nodes, connections, and parameters. Once your logic is finalized, you publish the graph to receive a standard Asset ID.

In your scripts, you interact with these graphs by loading them onto an Animator as you would a traditional animation. To drive the graph's internal logic, use AnimationTrack:SetParameter to pass real-time values—such as movement speed or state booleans—directly into the graph's variables.

local animation = Instance.new("Animation")
animation.AnimationId = "rbxassetid://123456789" -- Your Published Graph ID

local animationTrack = animator:LoadAnimation(animation)
animationTrack:Play()

-- Dynamic parameter updates via RunService
game:GetService("RunService").Stepped:Connect(function(_, dt)
    local currentSpeed = humanoidRootPart.AssemblyLinearVelocity.Magnitude
    animationTrack:SetParameter("humanoidSpeed", currentSpeed)
end)

Node reference

For details about each node type, see AnimationNodeType.

Global event rules

For all nodes and transitions, the following rules apply by default:

  • Events propagate upward from their source node through the graph. Each event carries a weight representing its source's influence in the final blend. If the weight reaches zero at any point, the event is silenced.
  • Nodes without custom event logic pass all events through unchanged; nodes that blend or select between inputs may scale the weight or block events from non-primary inputs (see per-node Event section).
  • Marker events that reach the top of the graph can be observed via AnimationTrack:GetMarkerReachedSignal.

Transitions

Several nodes in the Animation Graph (such as Select, Priority Select, Sequence, and Random Sequence) manage how animations blend when switching between active inputs. To prevent redundancy in the node reference, these behaviors are defined by standardized transition property groups.

Default transition

The baseline blending behavior applied to the node whenever it switches to a new active input.

  • DefaultTransitionDuration (number): The time (in seconds) it takes to fully blend into the new pose.
  • DefaultTransitionCurve (PoseEasingStyle): The easing function applied during the blend. Currently only supports PoseEasingStyle.Linear and PoseEasingStyle.CubicV2.

Transition override

Input-specific link properties that supersede the default transition. Duration and curve overrides apply when the node transitions to that input, except for BeforeFinished transitions, which use the outgoing input's overrides.

  • TransitionOverrideDuration (number): Overrides the default transition duration.
  • TransitionOverrideCurve (PoseEasingStyle): Overrides the default transition curve. Currently only supports PoseEasingStyle.Linear and PoseEasingStyle.CubicV2

Transition timing

For sequence node types, the following settings control when the sequence advances to the next input:

  • WaitFor (AnimationNodeWaitFor): Sets the condition for advancing. Use Finished (default) to wait for the current input to finish or complete a loop, or Trigger to advance when WaitForTrigger is true. Set the node-level default with DefaultWaitFor, or override it for an input with TransitionOverrideWaitFor.
  • When (AnimationNodeTransitionWhen): Applies when Wait For is Finished. Set the node-level default with DefaultTransitionWhen, or override it for the outgoing input with TransitionOverrideWhen.
    • Finished (default): Begins blending after the current input finishes.
    • BeforeFinished: Begins blending one transition duration before the current input finishes, so the blend overlaps the end of its animation. For example, a 0.2-second transition starts during the final 0.2 seconds of the animation.

RandomSequenceNode also supports DefaultTransitionWhen and TransitionOverrideWhen to control when blending begins.

For state machine transitions, see Transition properties.

Replication

Animation graph parameters and internal node state replicate automatically. The replication mode is determined by Workspace.AuthorityMode at the time the Animate script is created:

  • In AuthorityMode.Automatic: Parameters set via AnimationTrack:SetParameter replicate automatically to other peers.
  • In AuthorityMode.Server: The server drives the full graph simulation. All node states, such as elapsed time for AnimationNodeType.ClipNode, and graph parameters replicate automatically from server to clients. The owning player's client uses prediction for smooth local playback.

Sample Animate Scripts

To generate example scripts to drive an animation graph for a rig, use Graph -> Create Animate script in the Animation Graph Editor. This produces a script hierarchy placed under StarterCharacterScripts (for player characters) or directly on the rig (for NPCs):

Animate (ModuleScript)
├── RunClient (LocalScript)
└── RunServer (Script, RunContext = Legacy)

The Animate ModuleScript contains the graph-loading logic. The RunClient and RunServer scripts invoke it in the appropriate context. Which scripts are included depends on the use case:

Use Case Scripts Included Behavior
**NPC** (any mode) RunServer Server loads and plays the graph. State replicates to all clients automatically.
**Player + AuthorityMode.Server** RunServer + RunClient Server drives the graph authoritatively. The owning client enables PredictionMode for rollback-based local prediction.
**Player + AuthorityMode.Automatic** RunClient Owning client loads and plays the graph. Parameters replicate automatically to the server and other clients.

The following attributes are stored on the Animate script and configure its behavior:

Attribute Type Description
**GraphName** String Name of the animation graph asset.
**CharacterName** String Name of the rig the graph targets.
**SourceAssetId** String The published Asset ID of the graph. Used at runtime in published games.
**IsServerAuthority** Boolean Whether the script was created with Workspace.AuthorityMode set to **Server**. Determines the replication strategy.
**PreviewInStudio** Boolean When true (default), Studio play-testing loads the unpublished graph locally so you can iterate without publishing. Set to false to test the published asset in Studio. Note that this is currently not supported in AuthorityMode.Server.

Parameter replication in Automatic mode

When Workspace.AuthorityMode is Automatic:

  • The owning client drives player character graphs; the server drives NPC graphs.
  • Parameters set via AnimationTrack:SetParameter are automatically replicated to other peers. Multiple SetParameter calls within a single frame are coalesced (last-writer-wins).
  • No additional scripting is needed for parameter transport — the engine handles replication internally.
  • Other clients see parameter updates with a small delay (one send interval plus network latency).

Server authority

When Workspace.AuthorityMode is Server:

  • The server is authoritative for all graphs — it runs the simulation and replicates the full graph state.
  • What is replicated: Both parameters and internal node state, including elapsed time, current selections, transition progress, loop counts, and RNG seeds. This ensures all clients see identical animation behavior.
  • Player characters: The server drives the graph. The owning client's RunClient script automatically enables PredictionMode on the Animator, so the local player sees smooth, predicted animation that reconciles with the server on mismatch.
  • NPCs: The server drives the graph exclusively; clients observe the replicated state with no local simulation.

Driving parameters

Use AnimationTrack:SetParameter from every script that runs the graph:

  • NPC (any mode): Call SetParameter from RunServer (or any server Script with access to the AnimationTrack).
  • Player character in AuthorityMode.Server: Call SetParameter from both RunServer and RunClient. The server needs parameters to drive the authoritative simulation, and the owning client needs the same parameters to drive its local prediction.
  • Player character in AuthorityMode.Automatic: Call SetParameter from RunClient (or any client LocalScript with access to the AnimationTrack).

The generated Animate script includes a commented-out SetParameter block as a starting point. Uncomment and modify it to drive parameters from gameplay state (movement speed, humanoid state, input direction, etc.).

kid.simple: The Animation Graph Editor lets you mix and control animations by connecting boxes (nodes) with lines, instead of writing a lot of code. For example, you can plug a walk animation and a wave animation into an Add node so your character waves while walking. You make the single animations in the Animation Editor, then use the graph to decide how they combine and switch. Your scripts then just send in values, like how fast the character is moving, and the graph does the rest.
kid.analogy: It is like a DJ mixing board: each animation is a song on its own channel, and the graph's knobs and connections decide how loud each one plays in the final mix.
keyPoints: Open it from the Avatar tab with Graph Editor. Select a rig, then choose Graph, New to start a graph.
Right-click, Insert Node, Clip to add an animation, then set its Animation ID (the page uses default Walk `507777826` and Wave `507770239`).
An Add node combines a Base animation (like walking) with an Additive one (like waving). Connect its output to the Pose port of Graph Output.
Parameters are graph variables like `Speed`. Scripts change them with `AnimationTrack:SetParameter("name", value)`.
Publish the graph to get an asset ID, then load it on an `Animator` with `LoadAnimation` just like a normal animation and call `Play()`.
Marker events that reach the top of the graph can still be caught with `GetMarkerReachedSignal`.
Nodes like Select and Sequence blend when switching inputs, using settings like DefaultTransitionDuration (seconds) and a Linear or CubicV2 curve.

Graph, Create Animate script makes ready-made scripts. Who runs the graph depends on `Workspace.AuthorityMode`: the player's client in Automatic mode, the server in Server mode, and always the server for NPCs.

terms.node: A box in the graph that does one job, like playing a clip or adding two animations together.
terms.node-based: Built by connecting boxes with wires instead of typing code.
terms.Clip node: A node that plays one animation from its Animation ID.
terms.Add node: A node that layers an Additive animation on top of a Base animation, like waving on top of walking.
terms.blend: Mixing two animations so the change is smooth. A 0.2-second blend fades from one to the other over 0.2 seconds.
terms.blend tree: A set of nodes that mix animations together based on values like speed.
terms.parameter: A named value the graph reads, like `Speed` = 12. Scripts update it while the game runs.
terms.port: A connection spot on a node where you plug in a wire.
terms.weight: How much an animation counts in the final mix, from 0 (none) to 1 (fully).
terms.replicate: Copy from one computer to others so every player sees the same thing.
terms.AuthorityMode: A Workspace setting that decides who is in charge of running things: the owning player's device (Automatic) or the server (Server).
terms.prediction: The player's device guesses ahead so animation looks smooth right away, then fixes itself if the server disagrees.
terms.NPC: Non-player character, controlled by the game.

example.title: Send the character's speed into a graph
example.place: LocalScript in StarterCharacterScripts (player character, AuthorityMode Automatic)
example.code:
local RunService = game:GetService("RunService")

local character = script.Parent
local humanoid = character:WaitForChild("Humanoid")
local animator = humanoid:WaitForChild("Animator")
local rootPart = character:WaitForChild("HumanoidRootPart")

-- Load your published graph like any animation (replace the ID)
local animation = Instance.new("Animation")
animation.AnimationId = "rbxassetid://123456789"
local graphTrack = animator:LoadAnimation(animation)
graphTrack:Play()

-- Every frame, tell the graph how fast we are moving
RunService.Stepped:Connect(function()
	local speed = rootPart.AssemblyLinearVelocity.Magnitude
	graphTrack:SetParameter("humanoidSpeed", speed)
end)
explain: We find the character's `Animator` and its `HumanoidRootPart`.
We load the published graph's asset ID with `LoadAnimation` and play it.
We measure speed as the length of the root part's velocity, for example 16 when walking.
`SetParameter("humanoidSpeed", speed)` passes that number into the graph, which can blend from idle to run based on it.

watchOut: The parameter name in `SetParameter` must match the graph's parameter name exactly.
Plugging the waving clip into Base and walking into Additive. Put the main motion in Base and the layered motion in Additive.
Forgetting to connect anything to Graph Output's Pose port. Nothing plays without it.
In Server authority mode, player characters need `SetParameter` called from both RunServer and RunClient.
Using a transition curve other than Linear or CubicV2. Only those two are supported for now.
